To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the band discontinuities of the beta - FeSi2/Si system are temperature dependent.

(1) the conduction band offset between FeSi2 and Si is 1.0 eV and the valence band offset is less than 0.05 eV at room temperature; (2) the valence band offsets change sign when the sample temperature drops below 260 K.

the band discontinuities at the beta - FeSi _{2} /Si heterojunctions are very small, the valence band offset changes sign when the sample temperature decreases, the conduction band offset increases with temperature and the photoresponse is governed by the beta -Fe Si _{2} / Si interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrical properties of beta -FeSi _{2} /Si heterostructures and the photoresponse of these structures.
the photoelectric properties and the electrical characteristics of metal/beta -FeSi2/silicon structures.
the study of the photoelectric and electrical characteristics of FeSi2/Si interfaces and their temperature dependence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the band discontinuity at the beta -SiFe2/Si interface is not a constant but a temperature-dependent quantity.
the band discontinuities at the beta - FeSi2/Si interfaces are strongly dependent on the sample preparation method and on the temperature.
the band discontinuities of beta -FeSi _{2} /Si heterojunctions are very small, of the order of the thermal energy at room temperature, and that their sign is not univocal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photoelectric and electrical behaviour of the beta - FeSi _{2} /Si heterojunctions are governed by the interface quality.
the beta -FeSil2/Si interface presents a very high band discontinuity at room temperature.

, for thin epitaxial beta -FeSi _{2} films, the beta -Fe Si _{2} /Si interface is a good p-n junction with a large valence band offset, but the conduction band offset becomes negative at low temperature, which is detrimental to the photoresponse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photoresponse of thin beta -FeSi _{2} layers on silicon is dominated by the interface properties.
the photoresponse of thin silicide films is governed by the interface properties, whereas in thicker films the bulk properties are dominant.
the bandgap discontinuities are very small at the beta -SiFe2/Si interface and that the bandgaps are not aligned.
